reviews.comment: Very interesting lecturer. Provides lots of random extra credit quizzes AT THE BEGINNING OF CLASS so you have to attend and have paid attention to the previous lecture to get the points really. Exam wasn't too bad and he is very passionate about geotech. Only one midterm and one final, but the homeworks are a little annoying (sparse but lengthy).

Texas A&M is lucky to have Dr. MC teaching this class. His industry and research experience give him a technical and leadership authority not commonly seen in other courses. His notes guide to the detail what is important to learn. Could still hear his passion teaching when preparing for my FE exam. Always inspirational.

I was not expecting this class to be as interesting as it was, and for me to learn as much as I did. This is a foundation class for any civil engineer student. Yes, it is a lot of work, since you have lectures, labs, 
 and homework, but is strongly recommended to all CVEN students. Kudos to Dr. Medina for his lectures and for the extra-credit.

You don't find that stimulating environment in most of our classes. Much less at 8:00 am! Dr MC passionate teaching style makes you learn. His class is a must take. This is a lot of work, but that is compensated on how he sets his midterms, as if you were working already in a professional environment. He provides extra-credit opportunities.

Medina was very energetic for an 8AM, and always enjoyable. He was very passionate about the class, so that reflected in his teaching efficiency. HW was a little long, but doable. Labs were easy at first but got unreasonably long (not his fault). Open note exams made exam season a breeze.

You realize how important and how much you have learned from Dr. Medina's class when you see your results from from FE and PE exams. He will make sure you learn the material and understand the impact of the geotech discipline in the civil engineering profession. I strongly recommend taking his class!

Dr. Cetina is a great prof. This class is a lot of work. It is critically cumulative. You can't miss a lecture or a lab. But you learn a LOT! Never imagined hos useful and impactful geotechs are in the civil engineering profession. Dr. Cetina has a lot of experience He really wants us to learn. I strongly recommend taking his class!

At first I hated when Prof. Medina asked me to come to his office hours ready. He demanded to have a list of questions clearly defined, he asked if I had attended his lectures, if I have studied the class notes, and if I had a draft of the solutions. He said I had to learn how to approach a supervisor to ask for help. Nobody taught me that before.

Professor Medina brings his industry experience to the classroom. Even his exams replicate real applications and offer a real testing environment like if you were already seating in an office addressing concepts he insists we must know to perform well not only in the PE exam but in our future professional life. I strongly recommend taking his class

Dr. Medina is one of my professors that has shown the most dedication to his students to learn the class material. Very passionate & funny! He took the class as close to real scenarios where 'no partial credit is allowed' because 'there is no room for error in geotechnical engineering practice'. He offered plenty of extra-credit. Tough grading.

Dr. Medina-Cetina is an outstanding Professor. His industry and research experience are reflected in class. His lectures show fundamental concepts of geotechnical engineering and its applications. He does not provide partial credit, but offer multiple opportunities for extra-credit. He always finds the time to meet with students.

The Midterm had FRQs with 18 points a piece with absolutely no partial credit. Lets you correct the midterm for 50% back, which is fine. But, final is also no partial credit with FRQs at 20 pts a piece. He assumes that since he gives you 5 points on the final that this is fair. Claims this is all in the syllabus, it is not.

His grading is inconsistent and rather unfair. He does not offer partial credit on exams and claims that information was in the syllabus (it was not). In addition, he allowed me to go up and plead my case for an exam question and concluded that I "had everything clear but wants it more clear" and gave an F instead of the A I would of had otherwise.

This class was no joke.  There was a big focus on derivations, but Zenon is an awesome guy and cares so much about his students learning. I got a 16 on the midterm and he let us redo it for 75% credit back, and I ended the class with an A+. Its more work than the other profs but hes gonna help you out and youre gonna end with a good grade!

Dr. Medina is a terrible choice as a professor for this class. He gives very little partial credit on exams and quizzes. Often focuses on irrelevant topics rather than the curriculum. His quizzes and exams are made to be for a graduate student. I went to his office hours 3 times and would be told to find the answers to my questions on the book.

Average on the midterm was in the 20's or something. I got an 18 and the only way to curve it was to redo the whole test. Material on the exam hardly related to what we had done so far, and the quizzes are really hard for the most part (one every week). He seems nice, but just has no idea what he is doing.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Homework does not benefit the students. The midterm average was around 30 and had questions unlike anything we had seen before. We have been taught how to do 3 problems at most over the semester. No other section is as difficult. I earned an A+ in statics, so I learn the concepts easily. The (lack of) class structure is very difficult to follow.
